title: Relative pseudo-coherence is invariant under closed immersions
statement: Let $X$ and $Y$ be schemes locally of finite type over a scheme $S$ [def-pc-scheme], [def-pc-morphism-conventions], and let $i:X\to Y$ be a closed immersion over $S$ [def-weil-closed-immersion]. For every integer $m$ and every $E\in D(\mathcal O_X)$ [def-pc-derived-category], $E$ is $m$-pseudo-coherent relative to $S$ if and only if $Ri_*E$ is $m$-pseudo-coherent relative to $S$ [def-sfb-relative-pseudo-coherent-complex], [def-pc-derived-direct-image]. No quasi-coherence hypothesis on the cohomology of $E$ is imposed.

source.place: Tag 09VG, lemma-closed-morphism-relative-pseudo-coherence, restricted to closed immersions; its proof with T = affine n-space over S (the broader topological-embedding assertion is false; see report Source error)

proof.text: Write $f_X:X\to S$, $f_Y:Y\to S$, and $F=Ri_*E$; fix $m$. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis] choose an affine cover $S=\bigcup_a V_a$ and affine covers $f_Y^{-1}(V_a)=\bigcup_b W_{ab}$. Put $U_{ab}=i^{-1}(W_{ab})$. The affine quotient characterization in [def-weil-closed-immersion] makes $U_{ab}$ affine and the induced $i_{ab}:U_{ab}\to W_{ab}$ a closed immersion; these opens cover $f_X^{-1}(V_a)$. The embedding-existence clause of [lem-sfb-relative-pseudocoherence-all-affine-charts], applied to the locally finite type morphism $f_Y$ and the pair $(W_{ab},V_a)$, supplies $j_{ab}:W_{ab}\hookrightarrow\mathbf A^{n_{ab}}_{V_a}$. The composite $k_{ab}=j_{ab}\circ i_{ab}$ is a closed immersion by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-comp].

source.place: Tag 09VG, lemma-closed-morphism-relative-pseudo-coherence, affine reduction restricted to a closed immersion; Tag 09UJ and Tag 09VC for affine-space presentations

proof.text: For each $(a,b)$, [lem-pc-restrict-derived-direct-image-open] gives $F|_{W_{ab}}\cong R(i_{ab})_*(E|_{U_{ab}})$. Apply [lem-pc-derived-direct-image-composition] to $i_{ab}$ and $j_{ab}$ to obtain the derived-category isomorphism $$R(j_{ab})_*(F|_{W_{ab}})\cong R(k_{ab})_*(E|_{U_{ab}}).$$ Both cited results concern arbitrary objects of the unbounded module derived category, so this uses no quasi-coherence or boundedness. Absolute $m$-pseudo-coherence is invariant under this isomorphism: compose each local strictly perfect approximation with the isomorphism or its inverse; the cohomology isomorphism and surjectivity conditions in [def-sfb-m-pseudo-coherent-complex] are unchanged.

Assume $E$ is relatively $m$-pseudo-coherent over $S$. Apply [lem-sfb-relative-pseudocoherence-all-affine-charts] to $f_X$ with the affine pair $(U_{ab},V_a)$ and the particular embedding $k_{ab}$. It gives absolute $m$-pseudo-coherence of $R(k_{ab})_*(E|_{U_{ab}})$. By step 2 the same holds for $R(j_{ab})_*(F|_{W_{ab}})$. The covers $\{V_a\}$, $\{W_{ab}\}_b$ and embeddings $j_{ab}$ are precisely witnesses for relative $m$-pseudo-coherence of $F$ in [def-sfb-relative-pseudo-coherent-complex].

source.place: Tag 09VG, closed-immersion case using one common polynomial ambient scheme; Tags 09UJ, 09VC, and 09UI (definition-relative-pseudo-coherence)

proof.text: Conversely assume $F$ is relatively $m$-pseudo-coherent over $S$. Apply [lem-sfb-relative-pseudocoherence-all-affine-charts] to $f_Y$ with $(W_{ab},V_a)$ and $j_{ab}$. Its conclusion and step 2 give absolute $m$-pseudo-coherence of $R(k_{ab})_*(E|_{U_{ab}})$. Since $\{U_{ab}\}_b$ covers $f_X^{-1}(V_a)$, the base cover $\{V_a\}$, these source covers and the embeddings $k_{ab}$ are witnesses in [def-sfb-relative-pseudo-coherent-complex] for relative $m$-pseudo-coherence of $E$. This proves the equivalence for the arbitrary fixed integer $m$. All covers may be infinite and empty source opens cause no exception.
